in_arabic.name: مستتب
in_arabic.meaning: المستطب أو المستتب، هو من يعمل على تيسير وتسهيل الأمور
in_arabic.long_meaning: المستطب أو المستتب، هو من يعمل على تيسير وتسهيل الأمور، ويحفظ الأمور من الاضطراب والغموض، وهو من أسماء الله تعالى في القرآن الكريم، ويقال أن المستطب هو الذي يسهل الأمور وتيسيرها، ويحفظها من الاضطراب، وهو من أهم الصفات التي يُحفظ لها الإنسان في الإسلام، حيث قال الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أَللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى مُصَابِي وَزِدْنِي عَطَاءً مِن بَعْدِ ما أَصَابَني، وَأَذِلُّ عَنِ الحَسَناتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما فَعَلتُها، وَأَحِلُّ عَنِ السَيِّئاتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما فَعَلتُها، وَأُستَطِعُ الحَصْرَ عَنِ الشَياطينَ مِن بَعْدِ ما أُذِلُّوا لِي، وَأَعَطُّ الحَصِرَ عَنِ الشَياطينَ مِن بَعْدِ ما أُذِلُّوا لِي، وَأُعطِفُ مِنَ الحَسَناتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما نَظَمتُها، وَأُعَوِّفُ مِنَ السَيِّئاتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما نَظَمتُها، وَأُعطِفُ مِنَ الحَسَناتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما نَظَمتُها، وَأُعَوِّفُ مِنَ السَيِّئاتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما نَظَمتُها، وَأُعطِفُ مِنَ الحَسَناتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما نَظَمتُها، وَأُعَوِّفُ مِنَ السَيِّئاتِ مِن بَعْدِ ما نَظَمتُها".

data.cultural_impact: The name Mustatab holds a deep cultural significance for Muslims as it signifies a person who strives for excellence and righteousness in life. This name encourages the pursuit of knowledge, good deeds, and performing acts of worship that help cultivate a strong bond with Allah. Mustatabs are known for their unwavering dedication towards their faith and their commitment to embodying the virtues of patience, perseverance, and determination. This name further emphasizes the importance of individual effort and self-improvement in Islamic teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Mustatab is an embodiment of submission to the will of Allah. It signifies a person who is constantly yearning for Allah's pleasure, seeking His forgiveness, and striving towards achieving a higher level of closeness with Him. The name further reinforces the Islamic belief in the importance of the hereafter and the rewards that come with leading a virtuous life. Mustatabs are considered to be those who are always on the path of seeking Allah's love, guidance, and mercy, and their actions reflect the quintessential Islamic ideal of self-purification and personal growth.

historical_references.time_period: During the caliphate of Umar ibn Abdulaziz (Umar II) (683-693 AD)
historical_references.context: Mustatab ibn Abi-Sharik was a companion of Abu Hurairah who narrated Hadith. When Umar II came to power, Mustatab was given the position of treasurer. However, he was accused of embezzlement and Umar II ordered him to return the stolen wealth. Mustatab denied the accusation and invited Umar II to his house. When Umar II entered the house, he found the stolen wealth there. Mustatab confessed and was immediately executed.

historical_references.context: Mustatab ibn Jabalah was an Arab poet and scholar from the Banu Tamim tribe. He is known for his poetry and his work in the field of Islamic jurisprudence. He was a student of Imam Malik and is considered an important figure in the development of the Islamic legal tradition. Mustatab is also known for his role in the dissemination of Hadith and his support for the early caliphs.
